video_title: Doc Rivers Disses Giannis? Pat Bev Weighs In On LeBron, Giannis, Harden & more

quotes.speaker: Patrick Beverley
quotes.summary_phrase: Patrick Beverley defends Doc Rivers' perspective on Giannis Antetokounmpo
quotes.excerpt: Doc is historically a really good coach. He's coached the best of the best.
quotes.quote: Obviously when you are not a basketball player, not played the sport, not been in a locker room, you see it and it jumps off the page at you. I understand Doc in this situation. Obviously, Doc is historically a really good coach. He's put on an orange jacket in the Hall of Fame. He's coached the best of the best, he's won against the best of the best, he's played at this level. It's just his perspective. Even Coach Spo went on record and said yesterday that it's something that no one knows how to coach really because he demands so much attention when it comes to playing basketball. I understand it. Do I agree with it? Not all of it, but as a coach, you see weaknesses in your players throughout the whole roster.

quotes.speaker: Patrick Beverley
quotes.summary_phrase: Patrick Beverley discusses Giannis Antetokounmpo's basketball IQ and playing style
quotes.excerpt: I don't really think you need a lot of IQ when you literally taking the ball.
quotes.quote: I don't really think you need a lot of IQ when you literally taking the ball and the rim is here and you just throwing it in. That's what we seen a lot from Greek at an early age until now. It's a method of basketball that just can't be stopped. I think Doc Rivers' point was like, yes, that's good for Greek, but is that good for the team? I'm an advocate of you have to argue both. Greek has had some success, he has won a championship, and Doc River wasn't the coach. Doc River has won championships with not players like Greek. I think you just have to find the balance of both of what you really like.

quotes.speaker: Patrick Beverley
quotes.summary_phrase: Patrick Beverley on LeBron James' longevity and record-breaking field goals
quotes.excerpt: I think longevity matters. To be able to do something at a high level matters.
quotes.quote: I think longevity matters. To be able to do something at a high level, especially when it comes to being an athlete and when it comes to a demanding sport like basketball that's so competitive, I believe that how long you do something matters. For him to be able to even be in a layup line and do a reverse one-meal underneath at the age of 41 is impressive. When you come to 16,000 field goals ever made, he's breaking records that he makes it look so casual while doing it. We are witnessing literally greatness in front of us. When it comes to the goat, obviously it's Michael Jordan because I'm biased and I'm from Chicago, but LeBron James is, when I say steps, I mean itty-bitty steps right behind Michael Jordan.

quotes.speaker: Patrick Beverley
quotes.summary_phrase: Patrick Beverley dismisses the idea of James Harden coming off the bench
quotes.excerpt: I think that's ridiculous. What people have to understand is it takes a month or two.
quotes.quote: I think that's ridiculous. What people have to understand is it takes a month or two just for your legs to kind of kick in. I can still play. I know my beginning of the season, my numbers aren't going to be great, but I know once I get to December, January, end of January, my numbers are going to go up a little bit. It's a game of averages, and I think the averages are a way out. He's starting off slow right now, that's normal for James. He usually picks it up in the December, end of January, so I'm not too worried about that, not at all.

quotes.speaker: Patrick Beverley
quotes.summary_phrase: Patrick Beverley evaluates the Philadelphia 76ers and Tyrese Maxey's growth
quotes.excerpt: Tyrese Maxey has been the best player in Philadelphia probably for the last two or three years.

text_blocks.speaker: Patrick Beverley
text_blocks.text: If we are being transparent, Philadelphia just lost to Cleveland and it's probably one of James Harden's best games. But what Cleveland is doing, the best player on the team is Tyrese Maxey. In my opinion, Tyrese Maxey has been the best player in Philadelphia probably for the last two or three years consistently because Joel Embiid has been out with injury here and there. When you have a young leader like that at the point guard position, how dynamic he is, and I don't think a lot of people understand how much he works on his game. Me being in that locker room, I was the first vet that he had that he became an All-Star that first year. He's the best player. You add a person with Jaylen Brown, you add VJ Edgecombe, you have Embiid obviously, you have LeBron James, I think that makes his opportunities that much better.

quotes.speaker: Patrick Beverley
quotes.summary_phrase: Patrick Beverley credits Nick Nurse for the 76ers' team chemistry
quotes.excerpt: The first thing that jumps right off when you talk about anything with a team is the leader.
quotes.quote: The first thing that jumps right off when you talk about anything with a team is the leader, and that has to go to Nick Nurse. We do a disservice to coaches throughout the year. Nick Nurse got these two juggernauts, LeBron James and Jaylen Brown, in free agency and his ability to not only put it together, and we see what's going on in Miami how it has to take time. His ability to demand so much from his players, and I've been around him as a player and under his coaching staff, his ability to put those pieces together seamlessly so fast is very impressive. To have his team, guys who we talk about LeBron James, arguably one, two spots to ever do it, Joel Embiid, arguably if healthy the best center ever do it, Jaylen Brown, Finals MVP, to have these guys sacrifice so much, I think that's the really impressive part.

quotes.speaker: Patrick Beverley
quotes.summary_phrase: Patrick Beverley on the Golden State Warriors' veteran leadership
quotes.excerpt: They are able to expedite the growth of their young players because of so many greats.
quotes.quote: They are able to expedite the growth of their young players because of so many greats and veterans that they do have in the locker room. You have Al Horford who is still there, you have Draymond Green who is still there, you have Chris Paul, sorry, yep, he's not there anymore. We don't know what's going on with him. But you have these veterans that can expedite the mindset of these young players and that's what you see in the Warriors. I love his story. I love him working in the factory with his mom, just started playing basketball four or five years ago. I love his story, so you have a story like that put on a team like this, I think only good things happen.

quotes.speaker: Patrick Beverley
quotes.summary_phrase: Patrick Beverley on defending Luka Doncic and his high IQ
quotes.excerpt: I think it's more of his IQ, and that's what you have to give a lot of credit.
quotes.quote: I'm probably one of my toughest covers. I think it's more of his IQ, and that's what you have to give a lot of credit to, his culture and the European mindset. He's not going to settle. It looks like he's settling a lot when he shoots the step-back threes, but that's just his go-to. If he knows something is working, he's going to continue to do that and do that over and over. He's probably, when it's all said and done, historically he probably would be the best player to play pick and roll when his career is over. When he's healthy, he's put up Michael Jordan numbers in the playoffs.

quotes.speaker: Patrick Beverley
quotes.summary_phrase: Patrick Beverley praises JJ Redick's coaching of the Lakers
quotes.excerpt: Give JJ Redick a lot of credit also. I love credit in the coaches.
quotes.quote: Give JJ Redick a lot of credit also. I love credit in the coaches. His ability to allow Luka to play his game and still be competitive in the West is really impressive. Their record is really solid. They just got a dub last night and Austin Reaves, he looked like the smaller version of Luka last night against the Detroit Pistons. I think this brand of basketball that they are playing with JJ Redick, I think it's helping the guards that are dominant with the ball.

quotes.speaker: Patrick Beverley
quotes.summary_phrase: Patrick Beverley compares Luka Doncic's playoff numbers to Michael Jordan
quotes.excerpt: Luka Doncic's numbers in the playoffs are close to Michael Jordan.
quotes.quote: I agree with the Michael one. Rest in peace Kobe Bryant. Kobe Bryant wasn't really efficient, he shot a ton of shots, but he still got it done when he needs to get it done. Luka Doncic's numbers in the playoffs are close to Michael Jordan. That's just the honest to God truth. His numbers are very, very similar to Michael Jordan. So I think it is, sometimes we do get lost on what we love and what we don't like, but as older people as we know, it's a new generation and we got to step out our box a little bit.

quotes.speaker: Patrick Beverley
quotes.summary_phrase: Patrick Beverley on the importance of sacrifice from superstar players
quotes.excerpt: This should work not only because of the coaches, it's because of the sacrifice.
quotes.quote: You have Damian Lillard, you have Chris Middleton, you have Greek Freak, you have Brook Lopez, you have a ton of power. Besides injury, this should work. And this should work not only because of the coaches, it's because of the sacrifice that it comes from your superstar players. Now if your superstar players don't know how to sacrifice, you have to question the IQ of your players now. Maybe they didn't know, maybe I didn't teach you well, maybe they didn't understand it. Just like anything that we teach children coming up, coaching when it comes to that. So I don't agree, but I understand where he's coming from.
